stem:
Scientists have observed that crickets move their wings faster in warm temperatures than in cold temperatures. By noting the pitch of cricket chirps, it is possible to estimate the air temperature. Below is a graph showing 13 observations of cricket chirps per second and the associated air temperature.

[Image: Scatterplot of cricket chirp rate versus air temperature]

a) On the graph, draw in an estimated line of best fit for these data.

b) Using your line, estimate the air temperature when cricket chirps of 22 per second are heard.

Estimated air temperature: ____

codes.response: When template is lined up with the origin, the straight line of best fit should appear in the cut out section of the template for all air temperatures from 20 to 45 degrees Celsius.
The straight line of best fit does not appear in the "cut out" section of the template for all air temperatures from 20 to 45 degrees Celsius.
The graph is NOT a straight line, e.g., it is a curve or zig-zag line.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.

scoring_notes:
A: Codes for Line of Best Fit

Example of template showing allowable range
figure_description: A Cartesian coordinate graph showing a scatterplot. The vertical axis is labeled "Cricket chirp rate (Chirps/sec)" and has a tick mark at 0, followed by tick marks labeled 10, 15, 20, and 25 at equal intervals. The horizontal axis is labeled "Air temperature (degrees Celsius)" and has a tick mark at 0, followed by a jagged break line, and then tick marks labeled 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, and 45 at equal intervals. There are 13 data points plotted: (21, 15), (22, 16), (24, 14), (24, 16), (27, 15), (27, 16), (27, 17), (28, 16), (28, 17), (29, 17), (29, 18), (32, 20), and (34, 20).
